title: DuckStation can translate right-stick motion into PlayStation L2 and R2
summary: A separate trigger-button option maps horizontal right-stick thresholds to active-low L2 and R2 inputs, complementing the existing shoulder-button mapping without removing physical buttons.
heroAlt: Source evidence from DuckStation pull request #3692: Controller: Add option to use right analog as trigger buttons

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3692: Controller: Add option to use right analog as trigger buttons

blocks.text: Some early 3D camera controls predate a standard right stick

PlayStation games frequently put camera rotation on L2 and R2 because the original controller layout did not guarantee two analog sticks. On a modern pad, using the right stick can be more natural, but ordinary remapping cannot always express two digital directions from one axis while preserving the physical trigger buttons. MediEvil is the source's tested example of this historical control mismatch.
RightX thresholds synthesize the two active-low trigger bits

Pull request #3692 adds AnalogTriggerButtons alongside the existing shoulder-button option. When RightX crosses the negative threshold, DuckStation clears the L2 bit; crossing the positive threshold clears R2, matching the controller protocol's active-low button mask. The original L2 and R2 buttons remain available as well, so the axis acts as an additional input rather than replacing the game's authentic controls.
Always and digital-mode-only behavior prevent unwanted double mapping

The setting is an integer-list mode rather than a Boolean. One mode can apply the axis mapping only when analog mode and controller configuration mode are inactive, while another applies it regardless. Keeping trigger mapping separate from L1/R1 shoulder mapping lets users choose which historical layout they are adapting and avoids changing an existing preference's meaning.
Dead zones, mode switches, and simultaneous inputs need explicit checks

Test MediEvil with slow and fast RightX movement, center drift, physical L2/R2 presses, and both mapping modes. Confirm that neither trigger activates inside the dead zone and that moving directly from left to right releases one before pressing the other. Toggle analog and configuration modes while the stick is held, save and reload settings, and verify the older L1/R1 mapping is unchanged. Other controller types should not inherit the option accidentally.
The feature adapts a digital-era camera layout without taking controls away: right-stick directions supplement the original L2 and R2 buttons.
